sentence: This project studies how early-life exposures affect later-life risk of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, using methods that combine several data sets.
This project studies how changes in Wnt signaling with age affect hematopoietic stem cells in bone marrow and the healing of a fracture.
This project studies how transcription factors, which are proteins that turn genes on or off, are built to switch genes on.
This project studies how kidney injury happens in cystinosis, a rare disease, and works toward a drug that protects the kidney.
This project tests whether immune signals in a patient's monocytes can predict the side effects and results of T-cell treatment for blood cancers.
This project develops improved MRI technology to take pictures of soft tissues close to metallic implants in patients.
This project studies how a gene involved in heterotaxy syndrome shapes early heart cells and how its network relates to congenital heart defects.
This project offers screening tools and stem cell expertise to help researchers study eye diseases using retinal organoids.
This project studies immune responses to influenza vaccination in adults over age 75 to find signs of how well the vaccine works.
This project studies inflammatory lung disorders and allergic diseases to understand their basis and improve patient care.
This project tests an MRI method that records activity in the brain and spinal cord at the same time.
This project uses Drosophila to test whether gene changes found in patients with hypoplastic heart syndrome really cause the disease.
This project studies why a childhood brainstem tumor comes back, using a mouse model where a tumor-driving protein can be switched on and off.
This project tests how adoptive cellular therapy affects immune-suppressing cells in brain cancer and how brain irradiation might help it work.
This project tests whether one type of tumor stem cell produces the different kinds of dividing cells in a childhood brain tumor.
This project studies how a cancer driver starts and maintains tumors, using mouse models and human tumor models.
This project studies how a cell surface receptor senses mechanical and chemical cues to control breast tumor growth and spread.
This project tests whether reversing aging in bone marrow cells can prevent disease in the arteries.
This project studies how sex affects radiation damage to the intestine and tests a small molecule that may protect against it.
This project studies how the minor capsid protein of a virus passes through and inserts into membranes inside cells.
